bull.b: Minimal debt reduces interest and refinancing pressure, preserving more flexibility for clinical development and other operating needs. Although the company remains funding-dependent, low leverage avoids an additional fixed financial burden while Jasper works to advance its pipeline.

Completing the IgA nephropathy cohort and expanding into FSGS advances clinical execution while testing the therapy across multiple complement-mediated kidney diseases. Broader proof-of-concept could improve the pipeline’s strategic value and support future partnering or commercialization opportunities.

Retiring a majority of outstanding warrants can reduce potential future dilution and make the capital structure easier for investors and potential financing partners to assess. This improves equity-structure clarity, even though the transaction uses cash while operations continue to burn funds.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means Jasper cannot currently fund its activities from internally generated cash. Continued clinical development therefore requires careful cash management and likely external funding, increasing financing dependence and execution risk over the next several quarters.

Large losses relative to current revenue show that the business has not yet established an economically sustainable operating model. Until clinical programs generate meaningful commercial revenue or partnership proceeds, the cost structure can continue to consume capital and constrain strategic flexibility.

Negative equity indicates substantial accumulated value erosion and weakens the balance sheet’s ability to absorb further setbacks. The approved increase in authorized shares gives Jasper financing flexibility, but also underscores potential future dilution as the company funds operations and development.
